postData.contentHtml:
The insurance landscape in Australia and New Zealand is witnessing a fascinating transformation. Even as commercial insurance rates in the Pacific region experienced declines of 12-13% in late 2025 and early 2026, the top and fastest-growing insurance brokerages in both countries have defied expectations, boosting their revenue by a median of 20.5% in the 12 months to May 31, 2026.

This impressive growth, nearly double their median gross written premium (GWP) increase of 11%, signals a crucial shift in how successful brokerages operate. The era of simply competing on the lowest premium is over. Instead, the winners are distinguished by the unparalleled value they deliver beyond the transaction itself.

Katherine Wilson, chief executive of the Insurance Brokers Association of New Zealand (IBANZ), highlights this paradigm shift: "There is a clear shift underway from policy updates and rollovers to proactive risk and governance advisory." Clients are no longer content with basic renewals; they demand comprehensive advice and a partnership approach to understand and mitigate their specific business risks. Brokerages that are actively engaging with clients and reorienting their services towards this advisory role are the ones thriving.

Technology plays an equally vital role in this evolution. High-performing brokerages are adopting technology to streamline administrative tasks, allowing their brokers to dedicate more time to client interaction and strategic advice. While the pace of tech adoption varies, with challenges like legacy systems and AI integration, the industry's digital transformation is undeniable. Companies like Shielded Insurance Brokers in Queensland exemplify this, having built in-house technology to automate administrative work, thereby freeing up brokers to focus on client relationships and business development.

Another key differentiator for leading brokerages is their client-centric model. As Wilson notes, successful firms are driven by a shared vision of quality risk advice and unwavering client support during claims. Prestige Insurance Broker Services in Auckland, for instance, has moved away from the cheapest-quote model, focusing instead on continuous support and value delivery between renewals.

In essence, the top insurance brokerages in Australia and New Zealand are rewriting the playbook. Their success in a soft market is a testament to their ability to adapt, innovate, and prioritize client relationships and expert advice over mere price competition. This strategic evolution ensures they remain indispensable partners to their clients in an increasingly complex risk environment.
postData.title: Beyond the Policy: Unpacking the Growth of Top Insurance Brokerages in Australia and New Zealand
postData.summary: Despite a soft commercial insurance market, leading brokerages in Australia and New Zealand are achieving significant revenue growth by shifting focus from price comparison to proactive risk advisory and leveraging technology.
